title: Asia · breeds of the east
blurb: Japan, China, Afghanistan and the Fertile Crescent: the spitz breeds of the north, the flat-faced companions of the palaces and the desert sighthounds.

items.d: Large Japanese breed from the north, kept for guarding and hunting, and famously loyal.
Japanese mountain hunter, 33–43 cm, the smallest native breed and a national monument.
Ancient Chinese breed with a lion-like mane, a blue-black tongue and a stubborn, quiet nature.
Mountain sighthound from Afghanistan with a long silky coat and an aloof, independent manner.
The royal sighthound of the Fertile Crescent: long-legged, feathered and built to course gazelle.
Tibetan monastery watchdog, 25–28 cm, with a heavy coat and an independent streak.
Tibetan temple dog bred for the Chinese court: 20–28 cm, long hair and a flat face.
Chinese companion dog of the Han court, 25–33 cm, with a curled tail and a wheezing charm.
